Name Pronunciation engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume phonetic contact support covers storefront language. iOS, Contacts framework, and Connect actually separate pronunciation behavior from product-page copy:

  • Phonetic First Name & Phonetic Last Name — CNContact phonetic keys that tell Siri, Phone, CarPlay, and text-to-speech how to read a stored name. Controls in-device pronunciation — not App Store language.
  • Pronunciation / Pronounce Name editor — Contacts or in-app flows where users record or type how a name should sound. Your listing may show the editor; building pronunciation UI is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Siri & Phone readback — when a call arrives or Siri speaks a contact aloud, phonetic fields drive the spoken form. Marketing screenshots often show this outcome — distinct from visual Contact Posters.
  • CNContactStore & ContactsUI — APIs for reading and writing phonetic name components. Configuring phonetic persistence is engineering — AppLocale does not touch it.
  • Speech & pronunciation training — optional Siri training sheets some apps reference. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains pronunciation value to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of phonetic field support in the binary.

Working Name Pronunciation flows and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Name Pronunciation-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Phonetic name listings use vocabulary general Contacts hub guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's pronunciation fields — not a literal paste of US marketing:

姓名发音 vs 名字读音 vs 发音标注

US pages use "Name Pronunciation", "Pronounce Name", "Phonetic Name", or "Contact Pronunciation." Chinese App Store readers and iOS coverage use 姓名发音 for the feature badge, 名字读音 when screenshots emphasize spoken readback, 发音标注 for phonetic annotation or phonetic field entry, and 联系人发音 when the frame shows per-contact pronunciation in Contacts or Phone. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing pronunciation capabilities your app does not support.

Phonetic First Name / Phonetic Last Name fields

Screenshot overlays differ by editor step — phonetic first name, phonetic last name, pronunciation recording, or Siri training confirmation. Chinese buyers expect concise action labels: 名字拼音 for phonetic first name when appropriate, 姓氏拼音 for phonetic last name, 发音标注 for annotation fields, 教 Siri 正确发音 for teach-Siri flows. Mixing English "Phonetic First Name" with Chinese body copy on the same frame looks inconsistent.

Siri, Phone, and caller readback

Name Pronunciation value appears when Siri speaks a contact aloud, when Phone announces an incoming caller, or when CarPlay reads a name. zh-Hans overlays may use Siri 正确读出姓名 or 来电姓名发音 where each matches your frames — distinct from Contact Posters visual incoming-call art covered on the Contact Posters guide.

Do not conflate with Contact Posters or NameDrop

Contact Posters marketing shows photo, font, and color poster design — not phonetic reading. NameDrop marketing shows two iPhones exchanging contact cards — not phonetic field entry. If your app does both, scope each screenshot frame accurately: pronunciation editor on one frame, poster design or NameDrop exchange on another.

Terms like 姓名发音, 名字读音, 发音标注, and 联系人发音 each signal different intent from Contact Posters, NameDrop exchange, or general Contacts keywords.
